contract.words: I want $5,000 of settled cash within 30 days from residential moving companies only — selling something to moving companies, not becoming one. I can put in up to $500 and give it up to 2 hours a week of my time.

terms.proofCondition: USD 5,000 settled from residential moving companies within 30 days
exclusions: buyers other than residential moving companies

strategy.title: No plan yet: no product sold to residential movers has an established price, buyer demand or fulfiller
strategy.why: Three routes were discovered (movers website rebuild resold from a white-label developer, exclusive local-move leads, monthly Google Business Profile/review management). Verified research found no price that residential moving companies are shown paying (vendor list prices were rejected as out of scope), no buying signal, no close rate and no fulfiller who has agreed to terms. Brain's run reaches at most $0 of the $5,000 at prices buyers are shown to pay. A $5,000 plan cannot be called executable or conditional until a price and a fulfiller exist; a bounded test inside the $500 and 9-hour limits can establish both.

alternatives.title: Exclusive moving leads per lead
alternatives.why: Lead prices quoted by lead sellers ($15-$75) are sellers' claims, and paid-search cost per lead is unmeasured; 125+ leads within $500 of ad spend is not established.

alternatives.title: Monthly GBP/review management
alternatives.why: Needs ~17 first-month subscriptions; no price or close rate established.

noPlan.decisiveGap: No price that residential moving companies are shown paying, no buying signal and no fulfiller on terms exist for any route, so no plan reaches any of the $5,000.
noPlan.resolution: Costed experiment, $120 and ~2 owner hours, days 1-12: written quotes from 3 white-label developers (r1); 300 offer emails to residential movers at $1,500 with 50% deposit (t1); owner calls (t2). Proof: a developer quote <= $600 with <= 10-day delivery AND >= 2 movers pay a $750 deposit by day 12. Stop: no developer quote <= $600, or 0 deposits from 300 contacts by day 12 (4 sales then cannot settle by day 30). Continue: plan 4 sites as a CONDITIONAL plan on the measured close rate, with deposits paying the developer.

strategy.title: Movers website rebuild with quote form at $1,500, 50% deposit, white-label developer paid from settled deposits
strategy.why: A one-off product residential movers can buy without becoming a mover; 4 sales x $1,500 = $6,000 settled by day 28, with the only owner money at risk the $120 test tooling. Price, demand, close rate, developer terms and payout time are unknown and are measured by the test before any developer is paid.

answers.finding: Re-state as CONDITIONAL (the same experiment as its first phase), or name an evidenced constraint.
answers.resolution: Accepted: restated as CONDITIONAL; the $120 test (r1, r2, t0, s1, s2) is its first phase with proof/stop/continue.

answers.finding: Timeline: the card's timeToFirstCash is 14 days; with proof on day 12 and the 4th sale needing to settle by day 30, every sale must close by about day 16 and every site be delivered (<= 10 days per the proof's developer bound) by about day 26 so the $750 balance settles in the window. State the latest sale day and check it.
answers.resolution: Accepted: latest sale day is 16. Each deposit settles 2 days after payment (proof requires payout <= 2 days, r2), the developer starts then and delivers in <= 7 days, the balance is paid the next day and settles 2 days later: sale on day 16 -> balance settles day 28 <= 30. The card's 14-day timeToFirstCash is my own recommendation and is replaced by r2's measurement.

answers.finding: Proof needs >= 2 deposits but stop fires only at 0; 1 deposit by day 12 is undefined.
answers.resolution: Accepted: stop now fires at fewer than 2 deposits by day 12, and continue requires 2; there is no undefined band. If only 2 more do not follow by day 16 the plan stops at the sales made (each sale is profitable on its own).

answers.finding: Owner hours: the 4 calls (2 h) fit, but closing 2 more sales after proof plus approvals at 0.5 h/sale (card) must be counted against the remaining ~6.6 h.
answers.resolution: Accepted: owner hours counted: 2 h of calls (s2, days 7-12) + 2 h for closing calls and 4 scope approvals at 0.5 h (s3, days 13-16) = 4 h of the 9 h allowed, at most 2 h in any week.

If the payment route is a card invoice, fees (~2.9% on 8 payments of $750, ~$178) are missing from the ledger; settled cash would be ~$5,822, still above target. r2 should record the fee.
Contract v3 records ownerHoursPerWeek 2.1 while the owner's words say 'up to 2 hours a week'; the plan stays within 2 if scheduled as above, but the term should be corrected to 2.

review.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right stance and the revision fixes what the earlier review raised. Price ($1,500), close rate, developer terms and payout time are all unknown (card facts RECOMMENDATION; verified research rejected vendor list prices and interstate/all-mover counts) and each is gated by a bounded test with proof (>= 2 deposits by day 12 plus written developer quote <= $600 / <= 7 days and payout <= 2 days) and a matching stop (< 2 deposits), so there is no undefined band. Recomputed against contract v3: 4 x $1,500 = $6,000 settled by day 28 (3 would be $4,500 < $5,000); each $600 developer payment comes from a settled $750 deposit, so peak owner exposure is the $120 tooling, inside the $500 exposure cap; last sale day 16 -> delivery day 25 -> balance settles day 28 <= 30. Buyers are residential movers only (Maps 'movers' listings plus FMCSA carriers advertising local residential moves), and the product is sold to movers, so both exclusions hold. One balance default still leaves $5,250 >= $5,000.
findings: Settled $6,000 by day 28; exposure $120 <= $500; developer cost 4 x $600 = $2,400 paid from deposits.

Owner hours total 4 h (calls 2 h + 4 scope approvals x 0.5 h) of ~8.6 h; the per-week cap needs a schedule: calls in week 1, approvals A/B/C (1.5 h) in week 2 and D (0.5 h) in week 3 fits, but calls spilling into week 2 alongside three approvals would exceed it. State the weekly allocation.
If the payment route is a card invoice, fees (~2.9% on 8 payments of $750, ~$178) are missing from the ledger; settled cash would be ~$5,822, still above target. r2 should record the fee.
